_comment: Data-driven phase list for the client-reachability harness. Edit freely.
Each phase: name, desc, sets, load, relays, probe.
sets: the named runs that include the phase ('dry' = .5 plumbing run,
'full' = the .6 experiment). PHASES may name sets and/or phases. B0 is
the baseline and always runs first; the run fails closed if any B0
fetch fails.
load.mode: none | concentrated (onion D at every HSDir holding it) |
spread (the 'spread' onions; with common_hsdir, all at the one HSDir
that holds the most of them). load.pattern: steady (one fetch per
target HSDir every 1/rate s, so every HSDir sees load in every second)
or reuse (bursts of 5 fetches on one circuit, then a pause of 2 s or
more). rate_per_hsdir / rate_per_onion are fetches per second.
relays: list of {set, conf}, applied after every relay is reset to
DEFAULTS. set: all | none | serving:<role> (every HSDir holding the
onion) | serving_one:<role> | serving_clientfirst:<role> (the HSDir a
stock client asks first, so it is in the clients' fetch set). conf
tokens DEFAULTS / OFF / BUDGET expand at runtime; BUDGET is the BUDGET
env value. Options this tor does not know (HSDirFetchBudget on .5) are
dropped, so one file runs on .5 and .6.
probe.onions: roles D (loaded) and E (control). probe.attempts: per
onion: N, {ctor: N, arti: M} or {ctor: {D: N, E: M}, arti: ...}.
Requests are spread evenly over the phase, both clients at once. The
C tor probe can make about one request per 2 s in all (six client
nodes, one NEWNYM per node per 10 s), so keep its D+E total under
PHASE_S / 2.

phases.name: B0
phases.desc: baseline: no load, every HSDir at defaults

phases.name: C0
phases.desc: steady load on D at every HSDir holding it; enforcement off (FetchLimit=0) everywhere, small budget on .6 (observe mode: counters move, nothing refused)

phases.name: C1
phases.desc: .6: same load; FetchLimit=1 + small budget on EVERY HSDir (shedding everywhere; E's fetches are within their rate and answered first)

phases.name: C3
phases.desc: .6: the C1 setup with the load client at its maximum rate (30/s requested per HSDir; it reaches about 80 fetches/s in all), FetchLimit=1 + small budget on EVERY HSDir: lower lottery odds, the limit of what client retries recover

phases.name: C2
phases.desc: .6: same load; FetchLimit=1 + small budget on ONE HSDir that clients ask for D, others at defaults (failover)

phases.name: S0
phases.desc: .6: spread load: several onions at one common HSDir, each below its per-descriptor rate (4/s < 5/s), together over the budget; observe mode

phases.name: S1
phases.desc: .6: same spread load; FetchLimit=1 + small budget on EVERY HSDir (relay-wide budget, lottery among fetches within their rate)

phases.name: P5all
phases.desc: .5 stand-in: per-descriptor refusals (FetchLimit=1, Rate=1, Burst=1) on EVERY HSDir holding D, under the same steady load, so nearly every fetch of D is refused by closing its circuit

phases.name: P5one
phases.desc: .5 stand-in: the same refusals on ONE HSDir that clients ask for D (the stock client's first choice), the others at defaults; a refused fetch should fail over
